claim: Hamburg's two current 3-star restaurants are The Table Kevin Fehling and Restaurant Haerlin; 2-star list includes 100/200 Kitchen and Lakeside.
quote: 3-star: The Table Kevin Fehling, Restaurant Haerlin. 2-star: bianc, 100/200 Kitchen, Lakeside.

claim: Restaurant Haerlin at Neuer Jungfernstieg 9–14, executive chef Christoph Rüffer since 2002, 3 Michelin stars, Tuesday–Saturday 6:30 p.m.
quote: Restaurant Haerlin*** – Neuer Jungfernstieg 9–14, 20354 Hamburg. Tuesday–Saturday 6:30 p.m.–11:00 p.m. Executive Chef Christoph Rüffer.

claim: Haerlin is at the Fairmont Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten, dress code is smart casual, summer closure 19 July–16 August 2026 and 18–26 October 2026, also closed 1–9 March 2026.
quote: Smart casual. Closing dates: March 1–9 2026; July 19–August 16 2026; October 18–26 2026.

claim: Haerlin was promoted to 3 Michelin stars in the 2025 Germany guide, joining The Table Kevin Fehling.
quote: two new 3-star restaurants: Haerlin in Hamburg and Tohru in Munich.

claim: The Table by Kevin Fehling, single curved cherry-wood counter, 20 seats, HafenCity address Shanghaiallee 15, 20457 Hamburg.
quote: Shanghaiallee 15, 20457 Hamburg. Reservations: +49 40 22867422.

claim: The Table's single tasting menu costs €315 for 7 courses; 20 seats at one curved counter; sommelier David Eitel.
quote: Menu: €315 for 7 courses. 20 seats at a single curved counter. Sommelier David Eitel.

claim: Kevin Fehling's set menu is titled 'Das Tor zur Welt' (Gateway to the World), drawing Asian, Middle Eastern and South American influences on a French base.
quote: set menu dubbed 'Das Tor zur Welt' – 'Gateway to the World', combining Asian, Middle Eastern and South American influences with classic French-based cuisine.

claim: The Table is widely regarded as the hardest reservation in Germany; online booking opens roughly three months ahead and frequently sells out immediately.
quote: online booking opens only three months ahead at which point they are already full. The Table is the hardest reservation to get in Germany.

claim: 100/200 Kitchen, chefs Thomas Imbusch and Sophie Lehmann, at Brandshofer Deich 68, 20539 Hamburg, third floor of a 1926 brick warehouse; reservations via Tock, ticketed (carte-blanche) format.
quote: Brandshofer Deich 68, 20539 Hamburg. Advance ticket purchase required via Tock; binding reservations only.

claim: 100/200 Kitchen holds two Michelin stars since 2022 and the green sustainability star since 2020; menu is a seasonal surprise carte blanche aligned with themes like Water & Salt, The Season, Fire & Smoke, Field & Meadow.
quote: two Michelin stars since 2022 and the green sustainability star since 2020. Themes: Water & Salt, The Season, Fire & Smoke, Field & Meadow.

claim: 100/200 runs entirely vegetarian rotations such as 'Die Saison'; sister à la carte room Glorie opened in early 2024 on the gallery with vegetarian-friendly free choice.
quote: 100/200 vegetarian-only seasonal menu; gallery-level Glorie added in 2024 for free-choice à la carte.

claim: Lakeside is on the 7th floor of Hotel The Fontenay, chef Julian Stowasser, 2 Michelin stars.
quote: Lakeside, 7th floor of The Fontenay, chef Julian Stowasser, 2 Michelin stars.

claim: Lakeside address Fontenay 10, 20354 Hamburg; Tuesday–Saturday seatings between 7 and 8 p.m.; single 7-course tasting menu.
quote: Fontenay 10, Hamburg. Tuesday–Saturday, reservations 7–8 p.m. Seven-course tasting menu.

claim: Lakeside 7-course tasting menu around €225 + €160 wine pairing at the time of the review; chef Stowasser blends Asian, African, Middle Eastern and Indian influences on French technique.
quote: €225 tasting menu + €160 wine pairing. Eclectic blend of Asian, African, Middle Eastern and Indian influences.

claim: Lakeside earned its second Michelin star in the April 2023 ceremony under chef Julian Stowasser.
quote: Lakeside earned its second Michelin star on 5 April 2023 under chef Julian Stowasser.

claim: Haerlin's six-course tasting menu was customizable; reviewer scored 17/20 with service rated higher than typical three-star houses; lake-view dining room on the Binnenalster.
quote: Customisable six-course tasting menu. 17/20. Service rarely seen even at many three-starred restaurants. Binnenalster view.

claim: Haerlin offers a Chef's Table and a Sommelier's Table overlooking the dining room with vegetarian-friendly menus.
quote: Chef's table available; Sommelier's Table overlooking the dining room; vegetarian-friendly options.

claim: Haerlin's 6-course menu is €350 incl. water and coffee; wine pairing €205; non-alcoholic pairing €150; Chef's Table €425/person.
quote: 6-course menu €350 (incl. water & coffee). Wine pairing €205. Non-alcoholic pairing €150. Chef's Table €425.

claim: Two-star bianc (Matteo Ferrantino, Am Sandtorkai 50) closed permanently on 31 December 2025.
quote: bianc, HafenCity, permanently closed as of December 31, 2025.

claim: The Michelin Guide Germany 2026 ceremony is on 23 June 2026 in Frankfurt — at the time of this research the 2025 selection is still the active edition.
quote: Sterneverleihung 2026: 23. Juni 2026 in Frankfurt am Main.

claim: 100/200 Kitchen menu pricing sits in the €200–250 range with a separate €50 alcoholic-or-NA pairing ('Geleitzug').
quote: Menü €200–250; Geleitzug-Begleitung mit/ohne Alkohol €50 p.P.
